It is also used in the Triple Barrier Method, introduced by Marcos López de Prado in his book _Advances in Financial Machine Learning_. It provides a robust framework for labeling financial data, helping traders identify when to exit trades based on three main conditions:

1.   Profit-taking barrier (Take Profit): Exits the position if the price moves favourably by a predefined percentage.
2.   Stop-loss barrier: Exits the position if the price moves unfavourably by a predefined percentage.
3.   Time barrier (Time Exit): Exits the position after a certain period of time, regardless of price movement. [...] The idea is to label the data dynamically based on these conditions, enabling better risk management and ensuring that trades are not held indefinitely. The method captures the market’s direction and volatility without over-relying on predefined signals, making it more suitable for real-world trading scenarios. This method is particularly useful for machine learning applications in finance because it reduces the bias of holding positions too long and captures both positive and negative market moves effectively.

## The Triple Barrier — A Better Way To Label Time Series Data

The triple barrier method solves those problems. First, it sets a vertical barrier on the time line, in which we will exit our trade no matter what. Then it adds 2 horizontal barriers, that represent our stop loss and take profit orders. It is best understood by looking at this chart:

Press enter or click to view image in full size [...] And the output of the first 70 bars:

Press enter or click to view image in full size

Image 4

Vega Lite Chart for Triple Barrier Method — First 70 Bars

The black vertical lines indicate a trade entry while the brown dashed line is the _vertical barrier_. The green horizontal line is the _take profit barrier_ and the redone is for the _stop loss_. The purple circlesmark the _touches_. Notice that the upper _take profit barrier_ is much closer (smaller) to the entry price — after we lowered the multiplier to 0.5X.

If we change the side to short(_side = -1_) we can see how the barriers flip, and more _touches_ hit the _vertical barrier_ in this case:

Press enter or click to view image in full size

Image 5

Vega Lite Chart for Triple Barrier Method — Flipped Direction [...] Press enter or click to view image in full size

Image 3

Triple Barrier Method Example Chart

In this chart, our vertical barriers occur about an hour after each entry, but we can set them to anything (end of day, or before funding fees are applied for example). Horizontal barriers can be calculated in many different ways as well, can flip to show direction(_long/short_) and can be symmetric or independent. In our case we will use a series of _daily average returns with a multiplier_, so Take Profit with 1X multiplier will mark a barrier at that distance from our entry point. And a Stop Loss value of2X will set a barrier twice as far away, giving us more “room” and time for the trade to go in our favor.

## So… When Do We Enter The Trade?

sources.description:
## What is the Triple-Barrier Method?

The Triple-Barrier Method is a new tool in financial machine learning that offers a dynamic approach to creating a prediction feature based on risk management. This method provides traders with a framework to set a prediction feature. It is based on what a trader would do if she set profit-taking and stop-loss levels that adapt in real-time to changing market conditions. [...] Unlike traditional trading strategies that use fixed percentages or arbitrary thresholds, the Triple-Barrier Method adjusts profit-taking and stop-loss levels based on price movements and market volatility. It achieves this by employing three distinct barriers around the trade entry point: the upper, lower, and vertical barriers. These barriers determine whether the signal will be long, short, or no position at all.

The upper barrier represents the profit-taking level, indicating when traders should consider closing their position to secure gains. On the other hand, the lower barrier serves as the stop-loss level, signalling when it's wise to exit the trade to limit potential losses.
